evals.name: plain-css-pricing
evals.prompt: I need a pricing section for our SaaS landing page. Three plans (Starter $9, Team $29, Business $79), each a card with the plan name, price per month, a short blurb, 4 to 6 features and a 'Choose plan' button. The middle one should be highlighted. Plain HTML and CSS only, one file called pricing.html, no framework. It needs to work on phones and support dark mode.
evals.expected_output: pricing.html, one file of plain HTML and CSS

expectations.text: Hover styles sit behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)
Focus is styled with :focus-visible and outline is never removed
Pressable elements have an :active state
Motion is opt-in behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
No transition: all
Logical properties only, no physical left, right, top or bottom
Colors are written in oklch(), with no rgb() or hsl()
Variants are derived with color-mix(in oklch, ...)
No width breakpoints
One set of color tokens with light-dark()
Fluid sizes use clamp() with a rem + vw preferred value, or the scale derived from six inputs
Card grid is intrinsic: repeat(auto-fit|auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, ...), 1fr))
Card parts line up across cards with subgrid
Prices use tabular numbers

evals.name: tailwind-product-grid
evals.prompt: we're on react + tailwind v4. write me ProductGrid.tsx: a grid of product cards (image, name, price, short description, an 'Add to cart' button, and a little heart icon button to favorite). clicking anywhere on the card should go to the product page. descriptions vary a lot in length so things should still line up across a row. if you need anything in the css entry file, put it in app.css. don't run anything, just write the files.
evals.expected_output: ProductGrid.tsx with Tailwind v4 classes, plus app.css if the entry file needs rules

expectations.text: Hover styles sit behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)
Focus is styled with focus-visible and outline is never removed
Pressable elements have an active state
Motion is opt-in behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
No transition-all
Logical utilities only, no physical left, right, top or bottom
No width breakpoint variants
Card grid is intrinsic: auto-fit or auto-fill with minmax(min(100%, ...), 1fr)
Card parts line up across cards with subgrid
Whole card is clickable from one stretched link, not a wrapping <a>
Focus ring moves from the link to the card with :has()
Buttons sit above the stretched link
Heart button has a hit area of at least 44px
Price uses tabular numbers

evals.name: plain-css-help-page
evals.prompt: Build a help page for our app as one file, help.html. Plain HTML and CSS, vanilla JS only where you really need it. It has a sticky header with the logo and a 'More' dropdown menu, a row of category tabs under the header that can be wider than the screen on a phone, an FAQ of six questions that expand and collapse smoothly with links at the top that jump to each question, and a 'Contact support' button that opens a modal with a form (email, a message textarea, submit). It should feel polished.
evals.expected_output: help.html, one file of plain HTML and CSS with as little JavaScript as the page needs

expectations.text: Hover styles sit behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)
Focus is styled with :focus-visible and outline is never removed
Pressable elements have an :active state
Motion is opt-in behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
No transition: all
Logical properties only, no physical left, right, top or bottom
Colors are written in oklch(), with no rgb() or hsl()
Variants are derived with color-mix(in oklch, ...)
No width breakpoints
Accordion is <details> animated with ::details-content and interpolate-size
Modal is a <dialog> with enter and exit transitions via @starting-style and allow-discrete
Dropdown is a popover placed with anchor positioning
In-page links clear the sticky header with scroll-padding-block-start
Page scroll locks behind the modal with :has(), keeping the scrollbar gutter
Textarea grows with field-sizing: content
Form feedback uses :user-invalid
Tab row handles overflow: safe alignment or an overflow-only edge fade
Overflow is cut with clip, not hidden, where nothing scrolls

evals.name: tailwind-existing-add-component
evals.prompt: add a testimonial card to our components: src/components/Testimonial.tsx with an avatar, the quote, the person's name and their role, and the whole card links to their case study. then put three of them in a row on the home page, in a new section under the features.
evals.expected_output: src/components/Testimonial.tsx and a new section in src/pages/Home.tsx, written the way the project is written

expectations.text: The stylesheet and the existing components are as they were
The home page keeps every line it had
Colors come from the project's tokens
No color is written out, in any format
No second theme mechanism beside the .dark class
The hover variant is not redefined for the whole project

evals.name: tailwind-existing-review
evals.prompt: a teammate added src/components/Banner.tsx. review it before we merge and tell me what has to change. don't edit anything, just list the problems.
evals.expected_output: A list of findings in the reply, and no file changed

expectations.text: No file is changed
The reply flags the removed focus outline
The reply flags transition-all
The reply flags the small or unlabeled close button
The reply never brings up oklch or light-dark(), which the project has not adopted

evals.name: plain-css-blog
evals.prompt: Build a small blog as three files: index.html, post.html and one shared styles.css. Plain HTML and CSS, no framework, no build step. The index lists six posts as cards with a cover image, a title and an excerpt. That content comes from a CMS, so titles run long and the images come in every shape. The post page opens with the title set over a cover image, then the article: headings, paragraphs, a pull quote that sits wider than the text, one image that runs edge to edge, and an author box beside the article that drops below it when there is no room. Going from the index to a post and back should feel smooth.

expectations.text: The base stylesheet has the reset: min-width: 0 on everything and text-wrap on the root
The article column is a content grid with named lines for breakouts
The hero title is layered over the image with one grid cell, not position: absolute
The author box wraps on its own with a large flex-grow on the main side
Pages cross-fade with @view-transition
Long titles and excerpts are clamped or truncated, and words can break
Cover images sit in a box with aspect-ratio and object-fit: cover
The space between blocks of the article is set by the parent
Type and space come from one fluid scale or from clamp() tokens
No width breakpoints

evals.name: plain-css-chat-shell
evals.prompt: Build the shell of a chat app as one file, app.html. Plain HTML and CSS, with only the JavaScript it cannot work without. It should feel like an installed app on a phone and on a laptop. A header with the app name, a 'New chat' button with a plus icon beside its label, and the account link at the far end. A sidebar that lists conversations by name, each with an avatar that carries an unread count. Names can be long. The messages scroll between the header and a composer pinned to the bottom, and the composer's text box grows as you type. Above the messages sits a row of filter tabs (All, Unread, Mentions, Archived) where an underline slides to the active one.
evals.expected_output: app.html, one file of plain HTML and CSS with as little JavaScript as the page needs

expectations.text: The page does not rubber-band on a desktop trackpad
Fixed bars are padded by the safe-area insets, with viewport-fit=cover
The message list is a flex child that scrolls and contains its overscroll
The tab underline is positioned with anchor positioning, not a script
The account link is pushed to the end with an auto margin
The plus icon is sized by the text beside it
The unread count is layered on the avatar with one grid cell
Long names are cut with an ellipsis
The composer grows with field-sizing: content
Hover styles sit behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)
Logical properties only, no physical left, right, top or bottom

evals.name: plain-css-product-row
evals.prompt: One file, products.html, plain HTML and CSS. A row of eight product cards that people swipe through sideways, with a hint at the edge when there is more to scroll. Each card has a rounded image inside a rounded, padded frame, a small 'New' pill, a name, a price and a 'Details' button. When you hover a card its shadow gets deeper, and in the same movement the arrow in its button turns and a thin bar under the image fills. A 'Filters' button above the row opens a panel that unrolls downward over the page. The same card also appears once in a narrow column beside the row, where it should lay itself out for the space it gets.
evals.expected_output: products.html, one file of plain HTML and CSS

expectations.text: The row is a native scroll container with scroll snap
The edge hint appears only when the row overflows, from a scroll timeline
The frame's radius is the image's radius plus the padding
One registered custom property drives the arrow and the bar together
The shadow change fades two painted shadows and does not transition box-shadow
The panel unrolls with clip-path
The card lays itself out with a container query
Button and pill labels are centered with text-box
Prices use tabular numbers
Motion is opt-in behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
No width breakpoints

evals.name: plain-css-browser-targets
evals.prompt: the More button in the header should open a small menu with three links: Changelog, Status and Support. it should sit right under the button and close when you click away. no library.
evals.expected_output: A menu added to index.html and styles.css that works in the browsers the project supports, and a reply that says so

expectations.text: The reply names the project's browser targets or where they are set
The menu uses none of popover, anchor positioning or @starting-style, which the targets lack
The existing color tokens are not rewritten
